current.text: Adams is Houston's backup center behind Alperen Sengun.
Lloyd sees him only as a rebound streamer for certain matchups.
Lloyd expects him to sit back-to-backs, definitely at the start of the season.
He missed a large part of last season.
Houston is expected to use double-big lineups with Adams and Sengun at times.
With Adams back, Jabari Smith Jr. plays more power forward than center. Adams is part of a crowded bench with Marcus Smart, Reed Sheppard and Bogdan Bogdanovic.
Coach Ime Udoka plays his starters very heavy minutes, which limits bench minutes.
The Rockets have only 14 back-to-backs this season, which limits the number of games he is likely to rest.
With our March 28 end date, Houston has a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule, 10 games over weeks 19 to 21.
Houston is projected to win 54 games. The team is expected to be conservative in the regular season and not chase seeding.

durable.text: He is arguably the greatest offensive rebounder in NBA history and often needs two or three bodies to keep him off the glass.
He makes no threes and scores very few points, both far below the league pool.

note: Adams is not a draft pick in our 144-player auction. Both sites value him at 0 USD, with ranks of 397 on Yahoo and 329 on ESPN, and he gives nothing in threes or points. His only use is as a short-term waiver add for rebounds in good matchups. He had 8.6 rebounds in 22.8 minutes last season, but he is a backup now and should sit back-to-backs. Early in the season, check whether Udoka really plays him next to Sengun in double-big lineups and how often he rests.
